issue.title: Project Muse session-lifetime subagents into ACE instead of counting a fan-out as one agent
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-ha.4 (epic sase-ha, Meta Muse Code provider) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and deliberately listed as an explicit non-goal in the epic plan (sase/repos/plans/202608/muse_provider.md, 'Explicit non-goals': 'Do not project Muse subagents into ACE (see the follow-up note in artifacts)'), so it is new work rather than unfinished epic work.

WHAT IS MISSING: SASE currently models one 'muse exec' invocation as exactly one agent. When a Muse run fans out into subagents, ACE shows a single row and a single usage total, so a multi-subagent run is indistinguishable from a single-model run and per-subagent cost is invisible.

EVIDENCE THE DATA IS ALREADY THERE (established while implementing sase-ha.4 against the recorded R708.1 fixtures and a live authenticated run):
- The 'muse exec --json' stdout stream carries 'task.stream.linked' events linking a parent task to its spawned stream.
- The session directory Muse writes contains per-subagent 'subagent/<uuid>/session.jsonl' logs alongside the root 'session.jsonl' that src/sase/llm_provider/_muse_session_usage.py already globs.
- Session-log 'goal_usage_attribution' events carry 'owner.owner_type' and 'owner.requester_kind', which distinguish main_root usage from subagent usage. _muse_session_usage.py deliberately ignores goal_usage_attribution today (it would double-count against model_completed), so adopting it for attribution needs care not to reintroduce that double count.

SCOPE: decide the ACE representation for provider-reported subagents (rows, nesting, or a usage breakdown), parse task.stream.linked and the per-subagent session logs, attribute usage per subagent without double-counting, and keep the behavior provider-neutral enough that other CLIs with subagent fan-out can adopt it. Needs its own plan.

Filed by epic land agent sase-ha.land on 2026-08-08 while landing epic sase-ha.
